newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end weaker, hurt by U.S. treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end weaker, hurt by U.S. treasuries.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in moderate trade on Friday, with softer U.S. fixed-income markets and profit-taking on the week's strong gains weighing on prices, analysts said.

"It's nothing really that's specific to Canada. We got to a point in the middle of the week where the U.S. was technically stretched. There's also a little bit of concern going into Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony," said Arve Bendiksrud, a fixed-income analyst with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.72 to C$119.03 to yield 6.541 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 14/32 to yield 6.52 percent. The yields on the bonds moved from trading at par to a positive spread of two basis points.

Canadian and U.S. bonds opened the session weaker, with profit-taking hurting prices in both countries. The profit- taking came after the Canadian 30-year benchmark bond on Thursday traded with a record low yield of 6.472 percent. Given the move to record levels, analysts said the pullback in bond prices came as little surprise.
Bond traders in both countries were looking ahead to next week's public testimony by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve will give his testimony on the state of the U.S. economy to Congress on Tuesday morning.

Canadian bond traders are also looking ahead to next week's new 30-year Government of Canada bond supply. The Bank of Canada on Wednesday will auction C$1.3 billion of 8.0 percent bonds due June 1, 2027.

Speculation also remained in money markets that the Bank of Canada will soon raise interest rates. Dealers cited a weak dollar and signs of an accelerating economy as possible reasons for a rate hike.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.45 to C$109.20 to yield 5.999 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 11/32 to yield 6.24 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 24 basis points, unchanged from Thursday's close.
